The Nigeria Customs Service, Apapa Area Command, said it generated N302bn as revenue in October representing an increase of N20bn when compared with N282bn collected in September. In a statement on Thursday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Isah Sulaiman, explained that the figure shows a month-on-month growth of approximately 7.13 per cent. “The Apapa Area Command generated N302bn in October 2026, representing an increase of N20bn over the N282bn recorded in September 2026.This represents a month-on-month growth of approximately 7.13 per cent,” Sulaiman said. Sulaiman emphasised that the October collection marks another significant revenue performance above the N300bn threshold, following the command’s record-breaking collection of over N323bn in July 2026. According to him, the performance reflects the command’s continued drive to strengthen revenue generation while facilitating legitimate trade under the leadership of the Customs Area Controller, Murtala Mu’azu, who assumed duty on 29 September 2026. He highlighted that since assuming office, Comptroller Mu’azu has prioritised stakeholder engagement, operational efficiency and improved service delivery in line with the policy thrust of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, on consolidation, collaboration and innovation. Sulaiman stressed that the approach was reflected in the stakeholder engagement meeting in October, which brought together importers, exporters, licensed customs agents, shipping companies and terminal operators to address operational challenges, including demand notice delays, cargo clearance bottlenecks and other concerns affecting port users. He added that beyond the meeting, the CAC has also embarked on courtesy visits to key stakeholders and strategic partners within the port community. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. He maintained that the initiative is aimed at eliminating unnecessary bureaucratic bottlenecks, improving inter-departmental coordination and reducing processing time, while retaining the necessary compliance and control measures. Speaking on the initiative, the CAC of the command, Murtala Mu’azu, said, “Under my leadership, the command has intensified efforts to review and streamline the processing of transire, with a view to eliminating unnecessary bureaucratic bottlenecks, improving inter-departmental coordination and reducing processing time.” Nigeria records 25% export increase in two years – NPA Terminal operator seeks port modernisation, inclusive growth Ikeja Customs intercepts N6.19bn contraband goods in four weeks The CAC reiterated that the initiative seeks to ensure that the various offices involved discharge their responsibilities more efficiently, while maintaining the necessary compliance and control measures. “This initiative is also driven by my commitment to trade facilitation and the need to address operational inefficiencies that could subject traders to unnecessary delays and hardship. Traders should not suffer the consequences of avoidable administrative lapses or delays. We must identify challenges, address their root causes and adopt practical solutions that will promote seamless business operations, enhance service delivery and create a more efficient trading environment,” the CAC said. In furtherance of this commitment, Comptroller Mu’azu has directed that cargo examinations must be conducted strictly in accordance with extant procedures and the requisite documentation and authorisation. He has also emphasised that examinations must not become a source of avoidable delays and has cautioned officers against unwarranted, repetitive or unnecessary checks capable of frustrating legitimate business transactions. “Officers have been charged to discharge their responsibilities promptly and professionally, without compromising compliance, revenue protection or national security. These directives are intended to ease cargo clearance, improve turnaround time, and promote a more predictable trading environment while ensuring compliance with the Nigeria Customs Service Act (NCSA) 2023,” he warned. Mu’azu said that the command is also strengthening coordination among relevant departments and port stakeholders to address operational bottlenecks affecting cargo movement. He pointed out that in the area of enforcement, officers of the command intercepted a total of 437 sachets of cannabis sativa weighing 392.5 kilogrammes in 2 separate containers during the period under review. Mu’azu mentioned that the seizures comprised 162 sachets weighing 125 kilograms in container number MSKU0486747 and 275 sachets weighing 267.5 kilograms in container number TEMU6149358. “The combined duty paid value of the seized narcotics stands at N196.1m,” Mu’azu stressed. Mu’azu said that the consignments were jointly examined with relevant sister agencies, underscoring the command’s resolve to prevent the use of Nigeria’s maritime gateway for illicit trade and protect public health and national security. He said that the command remains committed to consolidating its revenue performance, strengthening enforcement and building stronger partnerships with stakeholders to improve the efficiency of port operations. “The command will continue to pursue a balanced approach that protects government revenue and national security while creating an enabling environment for legitimate trade and economic growth,” he said.
